Trait-Based Base Quantity Resolution System

Overview

The base quantity trait system provides a type-safe, extensible mechanism for resolving base quantities (voltage, power, frequency, current, etc.) across different model types in power system simulations. It eliminates hard-coded field name checks (e.g., hasfield(model, :basekv)) and replaces them with declarative trait-based dispatch.

This system is used in per-unit conversion and report generation, and is designed to scale to hundreds of stability simulation models with diverse base quantity requirements (e.g., generators with power ratings, synchronous machines with inertia constants, converters with frequency references).

Key principle: Models explicitly declare their relationship to base quantities via traits, and the system automatically resolves values through compile-time dispatch.

Problem Statement

The previous implementation used hard-coded field name checks to retrieve base voltages:

# Old approach (brittle, not extensible)
function _get_base_kv_vector(sys, model_name)
    if haskey(sys.external, model_name) && haskey(sys.external[model_name], :basekv)
        return collect(sys.external[model_name].basekv)
    elseif hasfield(typeof(sys.models[model_name]), :basekv)
        return collect(sys.models[model_name].basekv)
    else
        return ones(n)  # Fallback
    end
end

Issues:

  • Hard-coded field names: Assumes all models use :basekv field name
  • Not extensible: Adding new base quantities (power ratings, inertia, frequency) requires duplicating conditional logic
  • Implicit behavior: No clear declaration of which models own vs. inherit base quantities
  • Runtime checks: Field existence checked at runtime instead of compile-time

Need: A type-safe, declarative system where:

  1. Models explicitly declare their base quantity relationships
  2. Resolution logic is generic (no model-specific conditionals)
  3. New base quantities can be added without changing resolution code
  4. Compile-time dispatch enables optimization

Architecture

Trait Type Hierarchy

The system defines three trait roles for base quantity relationships:

abstract type BaseQuantityRole end

struct OwnsBase <: BaseQuantityRole end      # Model stores base in a field
struct InheritsBase <: BaseQuantityRole end  # Model receives from ExtParam
struct NoBase <: BaseQuantityRole end        # Model doesn't use this base

Semantics:

  • OwnsBase: Model has a field storing this base quantity (e.g., Bus has basekv::Float64)
  • InheritsBase: Model receives this base quantity from connected models via ExtParam system
  • NoBase: Model doesn't interact with this base quantity (default for all model-base combinations)

Core API

Trait Declaration (implemented by each model):

base_quantity_role(::Type{<:AbstractModel}, ::Type{<:ReferenceType}) -> BaseQuantityRole

Resolution Function (called by per-unit and report systems):

get_base_quantity_vector(sys::SystemModel, model_name::Symbol,
                         base_type::Type{<:ReferenceType}) -> Vector{Float64}

Dispatch Flow

User calls:  get_base_quantity_vector(sys, :Bus, BaseVoltage)
    ↓
Query trait: base_quantity_role(Bus, BaseVoltage) → OwnsBase()
    ↓
Dispatch:    _get_base_vector(sys, :Bus, model, BaseVoltage, OwnsBase())
    ↓
Resolve:     field_name = _base_field_name(BaseVoltage) → :basekv
    ↓
Return:      collect(sys.models.Bus.basekv)
User calls:  get_base_quantity_vector(sys, :PQ, BaseVoltage)
    ↓
Query trait: base_quantity_role(PQ, BaseVoltage) → InheritsBase()
    ↓
Dispatch:    _get_base_vector(sys, :PQ, model, BaseVoltage, InheritsBase())
    ↓
Resolve:     param_name = _ext_param_name(BaseVoltage) → :basekv
    ↓
Return:      collect(sys.external.PQ.basekv)

Implementation Details

Source file: src/powercore/base_quantity_traits.jl (215 lines)

Trait dispatch implementations:

# OwnsBase: Read from model's field
function _get_base_vector(sys, model_name, model, base_type, ::OwnsBase)
    field_name = _base_field_name(base_type)
    return collect(getproperty(model, field_name))
end

# InheritsBase: Read from external (populated by ExtParam system)
function _get_base_vector(sys, model_name, model, base_type, ::InheritsBase)
    param_name = _ext_param_name(base_type)
    return collect(sys.external[model_name][param_name])
end

# NoBase: Fallback for unused base quantities
function _get_base_vector(sys, model_name, model, base_type, ::NoBase)
    return ones(Float64, length(model))
end

Field/parameter name mapping (extensible for new base types):

_base_field_name(::Type{BaseVoltage}) = :basekv
_ext_param_name(::Type{BaseVoltage}) = :basekv

# Future extensions:
# _base_field_name(::Type{BasePower}) = :mbase      # For generators
# _base_field_name(::Type{BaseInertia}) = :H        # For machines
# _ext_param_name(::Type{BaseFrequency}) = :base_freq

Trait declarations (inline in model files, after @register_model):

# Bus owns base voltage
@register_model Bus
Powerful.base_quantity_role(::Type{Bus}, ::Type{PowerCore.BaseVoltage}) = PowerCore.OwnsBase()

# PQ inherits base voltage from connected bus
@register_model PQ
Powerful.base_quantity_role(::Type{<:PQ}, ::Type{PowerCore.BaseVoltage}) = PowerCore.InheritsBase()

ExtParam connection (how InheritsBase models receive base quantities):

# In pq.jl
const PQ_TERMINALS = (Powerful.Terminal(:Bus, :i),)  # PQ connects to Bus via :i field

const PQ_EXT_PARAMS = [
    ExtParam(:basekv, PQ_TERMINALS[1], :basekv, BaseVoltage(), PrePerUnit(),
             required=true, description="Connected bus base voltage"),
    # ... other ext params
]

The ExtParam system automatically populates sys.external.PQ.basekv by:

  1. Looking up PQ's terminal connection (Bus via field :i)
  2. Using indexer to map PQ instance → Bus instance
  3. Extracting basekv value from connected Bus

Multi-Terminal Device Handling

Current Status

Multi-terminal models (Branch, Transformer) connect to two buses but do not currently need per-terminal base voltages because:

  • Branch observations: Only power flows (ActivePower, ReactivePower), no voltages
  • Transformer observations: Only power flows, no voltages
  • No VoltageNominal observations require base_kv conversion

Current implementation:

# Branch declares InheritsBase trait
Powerful.base_quantity_role(::Type{Branch}, ::Type{BaseVoltage}) = InheritsBase()

# When resolved:
get_base_quantity_vector(sys, :Branch, BaseVoltage)
# → Looks for sys.external[:Branch][:basekv]
# → Branch doesn't define :basekv ExtParam (only :i_ide, :j_ide)
# → Falls back to ones() vector (unused)

Design Options for Future Models with Per-Terminal Voltages

Scenario: HVDC converter with AC-side and DC-side voltage monitoring:

ModelObservation(:v_ac, VoltageNominal, ...)   # Needs AC bus basekv
ModelObservation(:v_dc, VoltageNominal, ...)   # Needs DC bus basekv

Option 1: Per-Terminal ExtParams (Recommended)

Add separate ExtParams for each terminal:

const HVDC_TERMINALS = (
    Terminal(:ACBus, :i),   # AC side
    Terminal(:DCBus, :j)    # DC side
)

const HVDC_EXT_PARAMS = [
    ExtParam(:ac_basekv, HVDC_TERMINALS[1], :basekv, BaseVoltage(), ...),
    ExtParam(:dc_basekv, HVDC_TERMINALS[2], :basekv, BaseVoltage(), ...),
]

Usage in model's get_output_value():

function get_output_value(sys, ::Type{<:HVDCConverter}, var::Symbol, idx::Int)
    if var == :v_ac
        v_pu = sys.models.HVDCConverter.v_ac[idx]
        base_kv = sys.external.HVDCConverter.ac_basekv[idx]  # Terminal 1
        return v_pu  # Or convert to kV if needed
    elseif var == :v_dc
        v_pu = sys.models.HVDCConverter.v_dc[idx]
        base_kv = sys.external.HVDCConverter.dc_basekv[idx]  # Terminal 2
        return v_pu
    end
end

Pros:

  • ✅ Uses existing ExtParam mechanism (well-tested)
  • ✅ No changes to trait system needed
  • ✅ Clear naming convention (:i_basekv, :j_basekv or :ac_basekv, :dc_basekv)
  • ✅ Model has full control over per-terminal handling

Cons:

  • ⚠️ Manual extraction in get_output_value() (not automatic)
  • ⚠️ Naming convention implicit (not enforced by type system)

Option 2: Per-Observation Terminal Specification

Extend ModelObservation to specify terminal:

struct ModelObservation
    name::Symbol
    pu_type::PUType
    terminal::Union{Nothing, Int}  # NEW: Which terminal provides base?
    # ... other fields
end

# Usage:
ModelObservation(:v_ac, VoltageNominal, terminal=1, ...)
ModelObservation(:v_dc, VoltageNominal, terminal=2, ...)

Resolution:

get_base_quantity_vector(sys, :HVDCConverter, BaseVoltage, terminal=1)
# → sys.external.HVDCConverter.terminal_1_basekv

Pros:

  • ✅ Explicit per-observation terminal association
  • ✅ Type-safe (checked at observation definition)
  • ✅ Automatic in report generation (no manual handling)

Cons:

  • ❌ Requires changes to ModelObservation struct
  • ❌ More complex API (get_base_quantity_vector needs terminal parameter)
  • ❌ Overkill for rare case (most models have uniform base)

Option 3: Current System Sufficient (Chosen)

Recommendation: Option 1 (per-terminal ExtParams) when needed, Option 3 (current system) until then.

Rationale:

  • Multi-terminal voltage observations are rare in power systems
  • Most branch/transformer analysis uses power flows, not terminal voltages
  • Manual handling in get_output_value() is acceptable for specialized models
  • Trait system focuses on uniform base quantities (single value per model instance)
  • ExtParam system already supports per-terminal parameters (see Branch :i_ide, :j_ide)

Path forward:

  1. Current models (Branch, Transformer): No changes needed (don't use basekv)
  2. Future models needing per-terminal voltages: Add :i_basekv, :j_basekv ExtParams
  3. Trait system: Remains unchanged (returns fallback for unused bases)

Extensibility

Adding New Base Quantities

The system is designed for easy extension to new base quantity types needed for stability simulation:

# 1. Define new ReferenceType
struct BasePower <: ReferenceType end       # Device power rating (Sn)
struct BaseFrequency <: ReferenceType end   # System frequency (ωb)
struct BaseInertia <: ReferenceType end     # Inertia constant (H)
struct BaseTorque <: ReferenceType end      # Mechanical torque base (Tb)

# 2. Add field/parameter name mappings
_base_field_name(::Type{BasePower}) = :mbase
_base_field_name(::Type{BaseInertia}) = :H
_ext_param_name(::Type{BaseFrequency}) = :base_freq

# 3. Models declare traits
@register_model SynchronousGenerator

Powerful.base_quantity_role(::Type{SynchronousGenerator}, ::Type{BasePower}) = OwnsBase()      # Has mbase field
Powerful.base_quantity_role(::Type{SynchronousGenerator}, ::Type{BaseInertia}) = OwnsBase()    # Has H field
Powerful.base_quantity_role(::Type{SynchronousGenerator}, ::Type{BaseVoltage}) = InheritsBase() # From Bus
Powerful.base_quantity_role(::Type{SynchronousGenerator}, ::Type{BaseFrequency}) = InheritsBase() # From system

# 4. Use in per-unit conversion or reports
H_base = get_base_quantity_vector(sys, :SynchronousGenerator, BaseInertia)

Future Base Quantities for Stability Models

Base QuantityReferenceTypeFormulaUse Case
Base voltageBaseVoltageVb (kV)Voltage conversion (current)
Base powerBasePowerSn (MVA)Device ratings (generators, converters)
Base frequencyBaseFrequencyωb = 2πf (rad/s)Dynamic models, governors
Base currentBaseCurrentIb = Sb / Vb (kA)Converter controls, current limits
Base impedanceBaseImpedanceZb = Vb² / Sb (Ω)Network parameters
Base admittanceBaseAdmittanceYb = Sb / Vb² (S)Shunt compensators
Base torqueBaseTorqueTb = Sb / ωb (N⋅m)Mechanical systems, turbines
Base inertiaBaseInertiaH (seconds)Swing equation, transient stability
Base fluxBaseFluxΨb = Vb / ωb (Wb)Machine models, excitation systems

Example use cases:

  • Generator: Owns mbase (power rating), H (inertia); inherits basekv from Bus
  • HVDC Converter: Owns Sn (rating); inherits basekv_ac, basekv_dc from terminals
  • Synchronous Machine: Owns H, Xd, Xq; inherits basekv, base_freq from system
  • Wind Turbine: Owns Prated, Qrated; inherits basekv, base_freq

Integration Points

Per-Unit Conversion (src/powercore/per_unit.jl)

Current usage: Extracts base voltages from ExtParam system for coefficient calculation:

# In calc_pu_coefficients() (line 167-189)
Vb = if haskey(external_bases, :terminal)
    get(external_bases.terminal, BaseVoltage, ones(n))
elseif haskey(external_bases, :i)
    get(external_bases.i, BaseVoltage, ones(n))
else
    ones(n)
end

Future integration: Could validate models declare correct base quantity traits:

# Validate model owns/inherits required bases
required_bases = infer_required_bases(metadata.params)  # Based on PUTypes
for base_type in required_bases
    role = base_quantity_role(model_type, base_type)
    @assert !isa(role, NoBase) "Model $model_type requires $base_type but doesn't declare trait"
end

Report Generation (src/powercore/reports.jl:545)

Current usage: Resolves base voltages for VoltageNominal observations:

if pu_type isa VoltageNominal
    # Use trait system to resolve base voltage (no hard-coded field checks)
    base_kv_vec = get_base_quantity_vector(sys, model_name, BaseVoltage)
    return [to_report_units(pu_type, vals[i], config, base_kv_vec[i]) for i in eachindex(vals)]
end

Future Stability Models

Trait system enables diverse model types without modifying core infrastructure:

# Example: Synchronous generator model
@kwdef struct SynchronousGenerator{Tv} <: AbstractDynamicDevice{Tv}
    mbase::Tv      # Machine MVA rating
    H::Tv          # Inertia constant (seconds)
    Xd::Tv         # d-axis reactance (pu on machine base)
    # ... other fields
end

@register_model SynchronousGenerator

# Trait declarations
Powerful.base_quantity_role(::Type{SynchronousGenerator}, ::Type{BasePower}) = OwnsBase()
Powerful.base_quantity_role(::Type{SynchronousGenerator}, ::Type{BaseInertia}) = OwnsBase()
Powerful.base_quantity_role(::Type{SynchronousGenerator}, ::Type{BaseVoltage}) = InheritsBase()
Powerful.base_quantity_role(::Type{SynchronousGenerator}, ::Type{BaseFrequency}) = InheritsBase()

# Usage in per-unit conversion
Sn = get_base_quantity_vector(sys, :SynchronousGenerator, BasePower)     # From mbase field
H_sys = get_base_quantity_vector(sys, :SynchronousGenerator, BaseInertia) # From H field
Vb = get_base_quantity_vector(sys, :SynchronousGenerator, BaseVoltage)   # From Bus ext_param
ωb = get_base_quantity_vector(sys, :SynchronousGenerator, BaseFrequency) # System parameter

Design Rationale

Why Traits vs. Metadata Fields?

Traits (chosen):

  • ✅ Compile-time dispatch (type-stable, optimizable)
  • ✅ Clear separation of concerns (model declares, system resolves)
  • ✅ Extensible (new base types don't change resolution logic)
  • ✅ Type-safe (incorrect trait declaration caught at compile time)

Metadata fields (rejected):

  • ❌ Runtime checks required (slower, less type-stable)
  • ❌ Harder to extend (adding new base type requires metadata schema change)
  • ❌ Mixes concerns (metadata both declares and resolves)

Why Three Roles (Own/Inherit/None)?

NoBase role is essential:

  • Provides safe default (no error if trait unspecified for new model)
  • Enables validation (can check if model declares required base)
  • Explicit "doesn't use" clearer than implicit fallback

Example: If model uses VoltageNominal PUType but forgets to declare trait:

# Without NoBase: Crashes with "missing key" error (confusing)
# With NoBase: Returns ones() (safe fallback), could warn if desired

Why Not Single Lookup Function?

Rejected alternative:

function get_base_voltage(sys, model_name)
    if model_name == :Bus
        return sys.models.Bus.basekv
    elseif model_name in (:PQ, :PV, :Shunt)
        return sys.external[model_name].basekv
    elseif model_name in (:Branch, :Transformer)
        return ones(n)  # Doesn't use
    end
    # ... add new models here
end

Problems:

  • ❌ Hard-coded model names (not extensible)
  • ❌ Must modify for every new model type
  • ❌ Doesn't scale to multiple base quantities (would need separate function for each)
  • ❌ No compile-time optimization (runtime conditionals)
